svg.text: DigitLab v0.3 / an infimum need not be an attained adversarial radius
Exact clipped-box breakpoints for the same fixed linear model. No retraining or nonlinear certificate.
1 Lowest-index ties create two different boundary behaviors
Positive infimum, attained at the boundary
Positive infimum, error only strictly beyond it
A higher-index competitor cannot win a tie. A lower-index competitor can. No numerical tolerance decides this.
2 Exact per-row thresholds reproduce every earlier box decision
All 7,188 row/radius booleans agree, not just the four totals. Models, source data and old reports are unchanged.
3 First clean-correct examples of each boundary type, not a representative sample
For unattained infima, the error witness is strictly beyond the boundary, before the next clipping event.
Proof scope: exact real affine function of loaded binary64 coefficients, not every floating implementation.
Data/images: Alpaydin & Kaynak (1998), UCI DOI 10.24432/C50P49, CC BY 4.0. Perturbed images are adaptations.
Established piecewise-linear optimization. No new algorithm, perceptual guarantee, production OCR or MLP verification claim.
